sections.text:
1 Quisnam sit hic liber, incertum manet.
2 Tâbit ben Ibrahim Abûl-Hassan el Harrâni e stirpe Sabiorum vixit 833-891
p. C. Opus De motu octavae sphaerae a Gerardo Cremonensi, ut videtur, latine
versum cum sphaera Sacrobosci editum est Bononiae a. 1480, Venetiis a. 1521.
Cf. Steinschneider, Zum speculum, p. 387, § 43 a.
3 Ioannes Hispalensis Iudaeus notus est (vide infra) sed cur Ulgembus (?)
nominetur et quid sit liber inscriptus Flores eruere non potuit Steinschneider,
l. c., p. 73, § 33. — Flores Iohannis nonne sunt Flores Abû-Ma'sâr a Iohanne
Hispalensi versi (Suter, l. c., p. 29 sq.)? cf. tamen infra p. 94, n. 1 [Boll].
4 Steinschneider (l. c., p. 390, n. 47) hoc ad opusculum refert mathematici.
Tâbit ben Korra De figura sectore, arabice : Katta. — Tâbit ben Korra el Harrâni e
gente Sabiorum, vixit 826-901 p. C.; cf. Suter, op. cit., p. 34, § 66, et opusculum
illud Gerardus Cremonensis latinitate donavit. Cf. infra p. 89, n. 3, p. 91, n. 2.
5 Alpetragius vocitatus est Nûr-ed-dîn el Betrûdji, hoc est ex parva urbe
Pedroche non longe a Corduba in Hispania, qui a. 1208 mortuus est. Opus suum
astronomicum versum a. 1217 a Michaele Scoto post breve prooemium incipit
verbis Detegam tibi secretum ; cf. Steinschneider, l. c., p. 362, § 12, et Suter, op. cit.,
p. 131, no 325.
sections.en:
1 What this book is, remains uncertain.
2 Tâbit ben Ibrahim Abûl-Hassan el Harrâni from the stock of the Sabians lived 833-891
A.D. The work On the motion of the eighth sphere translated into Latin by Gerard of Cremona, as it seems,
was published with the sphere of Sacrobosco at Bologna in 1480, at Venice in 1521.
Cf. Steinschneider, Zum speculum, p. 387, § 43 a.
3 Ioannes Hispalensis the Jew is known (see below) but why he is named Ulgembus (?)
and what the book inscribed Flowers is Steinschneider could not unearth,
l. c., p. 73, § 33. — Are not the Flowers of Iohannes the Flowers of Abû-Ma'sâr translated by Iohannes
Hispalensis (Suter, l. c., p. 29 sq.)? cf. however below p. 94, n. 1 [Boll].
4 Steinschneider (l. c., p. 390, n. 47) refers this to the little work of the mathematician.
Tâbit ben Korra On the figure of the sector, in Arabic: Katta. — Tâbit ben Korra el Harrâni from
the nation of the Sabians, lived 826-901 A.D.; cf. Suter, op. cit., p. 34, § 66, and that little work
Gerard of Cremona gave to Latinity. Cf. below p. 89, n. 3, p. 91, n. 2.
5 Alpetragius was called Nûr-ed-dîn el Betrûdji, that is from the small city
Pedroche not far from Cordoba in Spain, who died in 1208. His astronomical work
translated in 1217 by Michael Scot after a short proem begins
with the words I will uncover to you a secret; cf. Steinschneider, l. c., p. 362, § 12, and Suter, op. cit.,
p. 131, no 325.

summary.headline: Astronomical Corrections and Ptolemy
summary.text: Discussion of astronomical corrections to the motion of the sphere of the fixed stars, Venus, and Mercury in works by Tebith and Iohannes Ulgembus of Seville. Alpetragius’s critique of Ptolemy’s principles and suppositions is contrasted with Ptolemy’s authority and Aristotle’s *On Heaven and Earth*.
